entities.text: High Court Of Kerala At Ernakulam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The second accused in C.C.No.716 of 1998 on the files of the Court of the Judicial Magistrate of First Class-I, Kochi, filed this revision petition challenging the concurrent finding of conviction and sentence passed by the courts below under Sections 16 (1) (a) (i) r/w Sections 2(ia) (a) (m) and 7(i)
of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and Rule 5 Appendix B.A.11.01.11 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate of First Class-I, Kochi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard.
3.

The prosecution allegation can be briefly stated thus:-
On 30.6.1998 at about 3.30 p.m., PW1, the Food Inspector purchased one litre of cow milk from the first accused.

The second accused was the nominee of A3 company,
which manufactured and marketed the milk.
After sampling as per rules, one sample was sent to the Public Analyst for analysis.
Ext . P17
report of the public analyst would show that the sample did not conform to the standard prescribed for the food item and was therefore adulterated.
Thereafter, on the request of the accused, the second sample was sent to the Central Food Laboratory for analysis.
Ext. P19
certificate of the Central Food Laboratory would also show that the sample did not conform to the standard prescribed for cow milk and was therefore adulterated.
4. Before the trial Court, PW1 to PW3 were examined and Exts.P1 to P28 were marked for the prosecution.
DW1 and DW2 were examined for the revision petitioner.

5. The learned counsel for the revision petitioner has submitted that since no laboratory for the analysis of the food item was defined and no validated method of analysis was prescribed as per the mandate of Section 23 (1-A)(ee) and (hh) of the PFA Act, Ext.P19 cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased by the Food Inspector was adulterated.
The learned counsel for the revision petitioner relied on the decision of the Apex Court in Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176] to buttress his argument.

entities.text: Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
6. In this case, admittedly, the laboratory for the analysis of food item was not defined and no validated method of analysis of the food item was specified as mandated under Section 23 (1-A) (ee)
and (hh) of the P.F.A. Act.

Therefore, Ext. P19 certificate of analysis cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased in this case was adulterated in view of the decision of the Apex court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra).

It was held by the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra)
C.D.Shaijan vs Food Inspector on 22 February, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22378891/
2 that since the Laboratories were not notified and the tests conducted by such laboratories were not admissible in evidence, no prosecution could be based on such report and the accused was entitled to get acquittal.

entities.text:
Pepsico India Holdings (supra)
C.D.Shaijan vs Food Inspector on 22 February, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22378891/
2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the decision of this Court in Gopalakrishnan v. Food Inspector [2013 (3) KLT 455], the court relied on the decision of the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) and found that the Public Analyst's report was not admissible in evidence and accordingly, the Court acquitted the accused.
The matter was referred to a Division Bench and the Division Bench also affirmed the said decision, submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor.

Even otherwise, in view of the decision in Pepsico India Holdings (supra), the conviction in this case cannot be sustained as no laboratory was notified and no validated method of analysis was specified as mandated under Section 23 (1-A) (ee) and (hh) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

For the above said reasons, the conviction and sentence passed by the courts below under Sections 2(ia) (a)
(m) and 7(i) r/w Section 16 (1) (a) (i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and Rule 5 Appendix B.A.11.01.11 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, cannot be sustained and consequently, I set aside the same.

In the result, this revision petition stands allowed setting aside the conviction and sentence passed by the courts below under Sections 2 (ia) (a) (m) and 7(i) read with Section 16 (1) (a) (i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and Rule 5 Appendix B.A.11.01.11 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 and the revision petitioner is acquitted for the said offence.
The bail bond of the revision petitioner stands cancelled and he is set at liberty.

Sd/-
B. SUDHEENDRA KUMAR JUDGE Scl/12.02.2016
